thumb.title: 110 for 4. Then 246 for 5.
thumb.sub: How New Zealand fought back on day 1

concept: A comeback told as two scorelines. India's best moment of the day (110 for 4) sits in muted grey and the stumps score (246 for 5) lands in white beneath it, so the swing reads before a single word does. Slide 2 is a partnership bar chart: three long bars for the stands that built the innings and a sliver of a bar for the 3rd and 4th wickets that added nothing, which is exactly where India's spell lived. Slides 3 and 4 are single giant numbers (115 runs in the last session, Bumrah's wicketless 0/37) that explain why the advantage slipped, and slide 5 sets up day 2. Cricket blue, type and charts only: no player photos, no logos.
caption:
From 110 for 4 to 246 for 5.

India had New Zealand in trouble on day 1 in Christchurch. Akash Deep and Kamboj took three wickets without a run being added.

Then Tom Blundell dug in. He put on 74 with Daryl Mitchell and an unbeaten 62 with Glenn Phillips. New Zealand scored 115 in the last session and lost only Mitchell, caught by Jurel off Washington Sundar.

Jasprit Bumrah bowled 19 overs for 37 runs but went wicketless. Debutant Gurnoor Brar took 1 for 52.

Wellington was a draw, so this Test decides the series. Blundell (53*) and Phillips (36*) resume on day 2.
